html:
SMTO-SKL-0004 — A Skill's API key needs a secure web address

GUID: c957d91f-e55f-4ae9-b671-89475dc3160b
Slug: skill-credential-transport-insecure
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: skl

What happened

  • SMTO reported that a Skill's API key could be sent to a web address that isn't secure. This is an older kind of message, so it doesn't prove SMTO checked the connection this time.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings from the More options menu, expand Details and tools at the bottom of the page, and select Skills. Then select Configure on the Skill that uses an API key, such as Web. That's where each provider's web address and API key setting are kept.
  2. For each provider with an API key, check that Base URL starts with https://. For Brave Search you can leave it empty to use Brave's standard address. An https:// address encrypts the key on its way, so others on the network can't read it.
  3. Select Save, then ask your question again. The provider uses the corrected address for new requests once it's saved.

What success looks like

  • Every provider with an API key shows a Base URL starting with https://, and your request runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off security certificate checks or trust an unfamiliar replacement address just to make this message go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A retained diagnostic (no current code path emits it) reports that a provider credential would be used with a target that is neither HTTPS nor loopback; current resolve_credential_reference accepts but does not inspect its url argument.

What this means

  • This retained template describes credential transport restrictions, but current resolve_credential_reference resolves the secret without using its url argument to enforce that condition. This retained alias has no direct current emitting producer. Related source establishes the current boundary only; do not infer that a historical guard ran or prevented provider effects.

Why this can happen

  • This retained template describes credential transport restrictions, but current resolve_credential_reference resolves the secret without using its url argument to enforce that condition.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the actual adapter's transport policy and emitting version before attributing this guard to credential resolution.

How to fix it

  • Do not rely on resolve_credential_reference for transport security; it ignores its url argument. Inspect the adapter actually in use (for Web, the Brave Search provider's base_url, default https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search) and make sure credentials go only to a trusted HTTPS endpoint or an explicitly supported loopback address. Never disable certificate verification to make the request succeed.
  • Inspect the actual adapter transport policy and use its supported trusted HTTPS or expressly supported loopback route; do not assume reference resolution enforces transport security.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected adapter demonstrably enforces its supported secure transport before credential use.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically disable certificate verification or trust an unverified replacement identity.
